# `property-added-optional`

New optional property

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `property-added-optional` (both directions), `property-added-optional-in-request`, `property-added-optional-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A new optional property in an object schema.

## Why this default

In requests: old clients don't send it, which is fine. In responses: clients that ignore unknown fields are fine; strict clients may reject the extra field.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

Options for this rule:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `strict-clients` | `false` | `true` raises the response side to `warn`, for clients that reject unknown fields. |

```yaml
rules:
  property-added-optional: info
```

## How to fix

Nothing to fix for tolerant clients. For strict clients, see the `strict-clients` option.
